newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor to decide on zinc plant mid-97.
newsitem.headline: Gencor to decide on zinc plant mid-97.

text.p: South Africa's Gencor Ltd will decide whether to build a 220,000 tonnes a year zinc refinery in South Africa's Eastern Cape province by the middle of this year, project director John Taylor said on Wednesday.
The mining giant is expected to complete a feasibility study by the end of March, he told reporters.
"The intention is to go to the board in June this year," he said.
Given a speedy decision, construction should start in July, 1997, with first production in January, 2000. "I am very positive, but there are a lot of loose ends to tie up," he said.
Port Elizabeth officials hope the 1.7 billion rand refinery will be the "anchor tenant" for an ambitious new bulk harbour which they propose to build at Coega, 20 kilometres north of the city.
Gencor has identified Coega as its preferred site, although other options are available in the area including the rival port of East London.
Coega's backers will need to move fast to meet the Gencor timetable.

Coega's project manager Doug Reed said when the feasibility study is completed the backers will seek government support to the tune of 500 million to one billion rand for infrastructure, notably construction of a breakwater.
The zink refinery would process 440,000 tons a year of zinc concentrate sourced from Australia, Peru, Mexico, North America and Europe.

Zinc produced is likely to be exported mainly to the Far East. Gencor's partners in the project are the state-run Industrial Development Corp and Japanese group Mitsui, by its Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co Ltd and Mitsui and Co Ltd units.
Kynoc, a unit of AECI, plans to build a fertiliser plant alongside the refinery using suphuric acid produced as a bi-proudt of zinc production.
Other companies interested in establishing plants at Coega include Pretoria Portland Cement Ltd, Samancor, Iscor, Afrox and Willard Batteries.
